issue: Hardcoded date assumption ('today' is June 16) in calendar
explanation: The calendar builds June 2025 with isToday=d===16 hardcoded. As soon as the real date changes, the 'today' highlight will be wrong, and the entire calendar is statically tied to June 2025 regardless of the actual current date. The page-sub also says 'June 2025' statically.
recommendation: Always derive date/time-based UI values dynamically. Display the month/year in the header using toLocaleDateString().
insights: Consider a small date library (date-fns) if calendar logic grows, and add prev/next navigation handlers (the buttons currently do nothing).

explanation: The 'Prev', 'Today', and 'Next' buttons in the scheduling screen have no click handlers, leading users to expect interactivity that isn't there. Same applies to the Calendar/List view toggle (only visual switching, no data swap).
recommendation: Avoid showing controls that have no function in a prototype unless explicitly labeled as 'preview'. Disable or remove non-working actions.
insights: If this is a click-through demo, add a small comment in the code to indicate intentionally inert controls.

issue: Misleading icon direction for negative spend metric
explanation: The 'Monthly Spend' stat shows '↑ 4%' but uses the .down (red) class because increased spend is bad. This is inconsistent — the arrow says up while the class implies down. Same pattern with 'Avg Cost per Employee' KPI using .down with '↑ $0.31'. It can confuse users who interpret arrows.
fix:
Either align arrow with the class (use ↑ with .up only for positive outcomes) or introduce a semantic class like .negative-trend, and reserve .up/.down for direction. Example:
↑ 4% vs last month
recommendation: Decouple direction (up/down) from sentiment (good/bad). Use color classes named by sentiment, not direction.
insights: Add aria-labels like 'increase of 4 percent, unfavorable' to convey context to screen readers.

issue: Inline onclick handlers and inline styles reduce maintainability
explanation: Numerous onclick="..." attributes and large amounts of inline style attributes are scattered throughout the markup. This couples behavior/presentation to markup, complicates CSP (must allow 'unsafe-inline'), and makes refactoring harder.
fix:
Move handlers to addEventListener using data attributes:
<button data-action="show-screen" data-screen="overview">Overview</button>
document.querySelectorAll('[data-action=show-screen]').forEach(b=>b.addEventListener('click',()=>showScreen(b.dataset.screen)));
Move inline styles into utility classes.
recommendation: Adopt a strict CSP (no 'unsafe-inline'); separate concerns via classes and unobtrusive JS.
insights: If converting to a framework (React/Vue), inline handlers become idiomatic; until then, prefer event delegation.

issue: Global search auto-jumps after just 2 characters with no debounce
explanation: handleGlobalSearch runs on each input event and forces the user to the 'Locations' screen as soon as length>=2. This is disruptive — typing a search like 'sea...' would yank them away from any screen on each keystroke, and would also do so when they may not actually want location results.
recommendation: Use debounce (e.g. 250ms) for live-search and let users press Enter for navigation. Provide a dropdown of suggestions rather than navigating away.
insights: Consider scoping global search across multiple entities (locations, invoices, approvals) with sectioned results.

issue: Cross-origin script tags missing integrity and crossorigin attributes
explanation: The Chart.js script is loaded from cdnjs without an SRI (integrity) hash. If the CDN is compromised, malicious code would execute on the page. The Google Fonts stylesheet is also loaded without crossorigin/preconnect, which both reduces security guarantees and impacts load performance.
fix:
<script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/Chart.js/4.4.1/chart.umd.js" integrity="sha384-..." crossorigin="anonymous" referrerpolicy="no-referrer"></script>
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com"><link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin>
recommendation: Always use Subresource Integrity for third-party scripts/styles, or self-host the assets.
insights: Consider bundling Chart.js locally for stricter CSP and offline-friendly hosting.

issue: Lack of <html lang>-aware semantic regions and accessible nav landmarks
explanation: Sidebar nav buttons act as navigation but don't expose aria-current="page" when active. The notification panel toggle doesn't update aria-expanded. Modals don't trap focus, lack role="dialog" and aria-modal="true", and the close X icon has no aria-label. Screen readers will struggle.
fix:
Add ARIA:
<button class="nav-item active" aria-current="page" onclick="showScreen('overview')">…
<div class="modal" role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-labelledby="addLocTitle">…
<button class="modal-close" aria-label="Close dialog">…
Implement focus trap when modal opens, and return focus to the trigger on close.
recommendation: Test with NVDA/VoiceOver. Use an accessible dialog pattern (e.g. focus-trap-js) and ensure ESC closes the modal.
insights: Also add keyboard shortcut handling: Escape to close modal/notif panel, Tab cycling inside dialogs.

issue: showScreen relies on parsing onclick attribute strings to set active nav item
explanation: The code uses n.getAttribute('onclick').includes("'"+id+"'") to determine which nav item is active. This is fragile (breaks if quotes change, fails if button has no onclick like Team & Access/Settings) and tightly couples markup with JS.
recommendation: Prefer data-* attributes for behavior linkage rather than parsing inline handlers.
insights: This also makes future refactor to a router/framework simpler.

issue: ESC key does not close modals or notification panel
explanation: Users expect Escape to close overlays. Currently the only ways to close the modal are clicking outside or the X. This is an accessibility and UX gap.
recommendation: Include Esc-to-close in every overlay component as part of your dialog pattern.
insights: Pair with focus-trap and aria-modal for full a11y compliance.

issue: Notification panel and sidebar overlap may occur on mid-width screens
explanation: The notification panel is 340px wide and positioned right. On screens between 901px and ~1240px wide, opening the notif panel could overlap the main content. There's also no backdrop/click-outside-to-close for the notif panel, so it's easy to leave open unintentionally.
fix:
Add a backdrop:
.notif-backdrop{display:none;position:fixed;inset:var(--topbar-h) 0 0 0;background:rgba(0,0,0,.2);z-index:140} .notif-panel.open ~ .notif-backdrop, or toggle a class on body.
recommendation: Use a consistent overlay pattern: backdrop + close-on-outside-click + Esc handling.
insights: Consider a slide-in drawer component as a reusable primitive.

issue: Chart.js instances are created without keeping references for cleanup
explanation: Each chart is instantiated via new Chart(...) but the returned object isn't stored. If you ever need to re-render with new data (e.g., filter selects), you'd hit 'Canvas is already in use' errors. The chartsInited boolean prevents re-init but also prevents updates.
recommendation: Store chart instances when you anticipate dynamic data updates. Provide a destroy()/update() path.
insights: Useful when wiring up the filter dropdowns currently present above the charts.

issue: Search input lacks label and form semantics
explanation: The topbar search input has only a placeholder and no associated <label> or aria-label. Screen reader users won't know what the field is for. Same applies to filter selects on the Locations page.
fix:
<input id="globalSearch" type="search" aria-label="Search locations and invoices" placeholder="Search locations, invoices…">
<select id="locRegion" aria-label="Filter by region">…
recommendation: Always provide accessible names via <label>, aria-label, or aria-labelledby.
insights: Use type="search" instead of type="text" to get the native clear button on supporting browsers.

issue: deliveries map mixes data types (array vs string 'holiday') causing brittle checks
explanation: In the calendar builder, deliveries[d] may be an array of strings or the literal string 'holiday'. The downstream code uses del.slice(0,2).forEach(...) which would incorrectly slice the 'holiday' string's characters if the explicit equality check were ever removed. This is fragile and easy to break during refactors.
recommendation: Use typed/discriminated unions for event data; in TypeScript, this would catch the mismatch at compile time.
insights: Even in plain JS, using objects with explicit types improves readability and reduces accidental bugs.

issue: Approval action buttons have no handlers — dangerous for a real workflow
explanation: Approve/Reject buttons in the Approvals screen are pure UI with no JS. If this becomes production code without backend wiring, a user might think they approved a $648/mo cost change. At minimum, prototype state should be persisted and confirmation dialogs added before any real submission.
recommendation: For financial/operational impact actions, require explicit confirmation, show post-action toast, and log audit trail.
insights: Consider an optimistic UI with rollback on API failure for snappy UX.

issue: Form fields in Add Location modal lack name attributes, required validation, and id/label association
explanation: All inputs in the Add Location and Bulk Schedule modals use <label> visually adjacent but without for/id linking, so clicking the label doesn't focus the input. There are no required attributes, no client-side validation, and no name attributes for form submission.
fix:
<label class="form-label" for="loc-name">Location Name</label>
<input id="loc-name" name="locationName" type="text" class="form-input" required>
Also wrap in <form onsubmit="return validateAndSave(event)"> to leverage native validation.
recommendation: Always pair <label for> with input id; mark required fields; submit via <form> for keyboard Enter handling and browser validation.
insights: Add inline error messaging and aria-invalid for accessibility.
